classification.difficultyReason: Calculate interest separately for each year, distinguishing annual compounding from twelve monthly compounding periods per year.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Mr Yang invested $\$90\,000$ at a compound interest rate of $6\%$ p.a. for three years. The tax office wants to know exactly how much interest he earned each year. Calculate these figures for Mr Yang. Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
Each year's interest is $6\%$ of the balance at the beginning of that year.

$$\begin{align*}I_1&=90\,000\times0.06\\I_1&=\$5400.00\\I_2&=90\,000\times1.06\times0.06\\I_2&=\$5724.00\\I_3&=90\,000\times1.06^2\times0.06\\I_3&=\$6067.44\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Repeat these calculations with the rate of interest of $0.5\%$ per month.

answer.short:
Year 1: $\$5551.00$; year 2: $\$5893.38$; year 3: $\$6256.87$.

Use twelve monthly compounding periods for each year and subtract consecutive year-end balances.
answer.worked:
There are twelve compounding periods per year, with multiplier $1.005$ per month. Each year's interest is the difference between its closing and opening balances. Keep unrounded balances until the final answers.

$$\begin{align*}I_1&=90\,000(1.005)^{12}-90\,000\\I_1&\approx\$5551.00\\I_2&=90\,000(1.005)^{24}-90\,000(1.005)^{12}\\I_2&\approx\$5893.38\\I_3&=90\,000(1.005)^{36}-90\,000(1.005)^{24}\\I_3&\approx\$6256.87\end{align*}$$
